research_question: Does content-aware source selection improve domain coverage and retrieval quality compared with random source selection when both are evaluated against the same human-reviewed (frozen) benchmark?

hypotheses.H1_coverage: QUALITY_SELECTED corpora answer more of the frozen benchmark's questions than RANDOM_BASELINE corpora at equal N.
hypotheses.H2_retrieval: On the common answerable-question intersection of a QUALITY/RANDOM pair, QUALITY_SELECTED achieves equal or higher Recall@K / MRR / NDCG (paired comparison).
hypotheses.H3_efficiency: QUALITY_SELECTED reaches a target coverage with fewer corpus characters than RANDOM_BASELINE.

independent_variable: source-selection strategy (QUALITY_SELECTED vs RANDOM_BASELINE) and corpus size N
controlled_variables: frozen benchmark version (pinned by id at run time)
evaluation protocol (strict, explicit ground truth only)

candidate_pool.note: Same frozen pool as v1/v2 for comparability.

seed_note: RANDOM_BASELINE selection uses random.Random(seed).sample(pool, N) — deterministic per seed. Each seed produces an independent random arm; QUALITY_SELECTED is seed-independent.

benchmark_requirement.description: The runner REFUSES to execute unless --benchmark-version names a FROZEN BenchmarkVersion of the KB. This enforces the Phase A rule: official experiments only on human-reviewed benchmarks.
benchmark_requirement.ground_truth_caveat: Superseded only when the frozen benchmark version is approved by a human reviewer; until then no v3 run may start.

comparison_methodology.paired_intersection: Metrics are compared between two runs ONLY on the intersection of their answerable-question sets, recomputed per question from the run's per_question records.
comparison_methodology.coverage_separate: Coverage is reported separately and is never mixed into retrieval metrics.
comparison_methodology.aggregate_caveat: Raw aggregate metrics across runs with different answerable sets are reported but flagged as NOT directly comparable.
